sections.text: Let the student of spirituality try unceasingly to concentrate his mind; Let him live in seclusion, absolutely alone, with mind and personality controlled, free from desire and without possessions.
Having chosen a holy place, let him sit in a firm posture on a seat, neither too high nor too low, and covered with a grass mat, a deer skin and a cloth.
Seated thus, his mind concentrated, its functions controlled and his senses governed, let him practise meditation for the purification of his lower nature.

We had been discussing chapter six, Dhyana Yoga Yoga of Meditation. In first five chapters we learned about ourselves. We learned the terms Yogi and sannyasi.
So in this chapter weve learned so far that the one who is acting in this world without depending on the fruits of actions is a yogi and also a sannyasi. Because a sannyasi cannot be a sannyasi unless he has given up all the sense of agency. A Yogi cannot be a yogi until he gives up all the Sankalpas Sarva Sankalpa Sanyasi.
So both reach the same state of becoming equanimous to all the happenings around them. And Bhagavan said, the one who has not yet achieved the state of Yoga, Arudha. So we are seekers, the seeker.
The prescription is to selfless actions. Karma Karanam Uchathe. But one, you are established in Yoga then Shamah Karanamuchate then controlling your mind is your pursuit to achieve the higher level. How do I know that I have become established in yoga? Once you get detached from your actions and also the sense objects -- when you are completely detached from the world of objects and the world of your activities -- in other words, you are functioning but not having that attachment to it.
When you achieve that state, Sarva Sankalpa Sannyasi, there are no aspirations to achieve anything or to accomplish anything. That seems like a pretty dangerous state of mind. But in other words, you know what needs to be done and you will be doing it, but without any anxiety about what will come out of it.
When you reach that state, then you are Yogarudha. But how do I get to that point? Bhagavan said, let yourself lift yourself. Let your higher self lift this lower self to a level where they both become aligned with each other.
Right now my identification is with the lower self, which we have defined as my body, mind, and intellect. This limited being I consider to be me in all my pursuits. I try to achieve happiness through this limited being.
But being limited, it is limited. It cannot achieve infinite happiness. But I miss that equation: something finite cannot achieve anything infinite.
I am constantly pursuing infinite happiness, infinite bliss, an infinite state where there is no sorrow, using equipment which is finite. Once you align yourself with that higher self which is infinite, you will achieve your goal. So let your higher self lift your lower self to a level aligned with it.
And then came the caution: that higher self can be your enemy or a friend. Depending on whether I have control over my self, my senses, my mind. If I have no control over mind and senses, higher self enable me to do whatever my lower self wants to do and then it will be a disaster.
So now the higher self is acting as an enemy because its allowing me to do things which are not good for me. So once I have understood that the higher self is there to enable me to achieve higher goals and align with it, it will become my friend. Once I have achieved that state, what will happen? We have learned that then one becomes in a state of equanimity.
His self remains same in a Sita, Ushna, Sukhada, Kamana or Pramana. At the level of physical being, at the level of mental being or intellectual being. My connection with the higher remains the same.
In other words, that I do not identify with whats happening with my body, mind and intellect. I continue to identify with my higher self which remains as a witness to whats happening. Therefore it is not getting affected.
When I see that things are happening to people around me but I am not affected, then I am a witness. I heard a long time ago a definition of recession and depression: when your neighbour gets laid off, its a recession. When you get laid off, its a depression.
As long as Im not affected, Its a good topic to talk about. So as long as I dont identify with whats happening, it does not affect me. So as long as my self is constantly identifying with the higher self, whatever happening at the physical level, mental level, intellectual level, it does not get affected.
Then he will also become one with all beings in their relationship. Gnana Vignana Truptatma Kutastha Vijitendriyah Yukta iti uchyate Yogi Sama Loshta Ashma Kanchanah. He sees everything in the physical world as essentially the same. He knows that there is no inherent value in anything.
Value is what I assign the value to. As long as I know this is a million dollar Diamond. There is a value because I can sell it.
But if I do not know what their value is, it is no different than a costume jewelry. So values are what I assign to it, the world assigned to it. But there is no inherent value in anything or being.
Thats the person with the alignment of the higher self. Then we are saying that even in his relationship, Suhan, mitra, Hari, udasin, madhyas, all different types of people we deal with in our life. Some are friends, some are foes, some are indifferent, some are relatives.
But we see them all equally. In other words, they are all manifestation of the same self. So this is the state described of a yogi.
But we are not at this stage. The prescription is: continue doing selfless actions for the purification of your mind and intellect. When the internal instrument becomes pure, you start seeing your connection with the higher.
That inner voice which is so feeble right now, youll hear loud and clear. How to get there is what the next few verses tell us -- a detailed description of the practices one can follow. Now, last time we had this discussion about whether meditation is for yogis only or for anybody.
And there is a question about whether we understand what meditation is. Meditation is the final state. If you take Patanjalis Yoga Sutra, there are eight different stages before you get to the state of meditation: Yama, Niyama, Asana, Pranayama, Pratyahara, Dharana, Dhyana, and Samadhi.
We have to go through all these different steps to get to a level where we are ready for meditation. But that does not mean you dont have to start somewhere. You have to start at some place, wherever you are in your journey, one step at a time.
And then you have to discipline yourself, which is where Yama (restraint) and Niyama (observance) come in. In anything, what really matters is constant practice. When I used to work for large companies, the marketing people, before you go for a presentation, would say, Lets have a rehearsal. Some of us would feel, Ive been doing it for years, why do I have to practice? They say, no, no, Rajan, do the rehearsal one time and we are done.
Practice, practice and practice some more. Then only you will be able to present it flawlessly when you go there. So in anything, practice, practice and practice some more is the key.
Most of us will say, I tried that. And when obviously its not working for me. But how long have you tried? A couple of days.
Obviously there is no way to judge what you can achieve if you continue to practice. But how you practice is just as important. We sometimes say that somebody has 10 years of experience, but it may be one year of experience repeated ten times.
He never progressed beyond the very first year. Whatever he learned, he keeps doing for the next 10 years and says, I have 10 years of experience. So you have to learn how to start in the right manner and then make progress. The next three verses teach us how to start that journey.
Yogi yunjita satatam atmanam rahasi sthitah, ekaki yata chittatma nirashih aparigrahah. This is the description of how the yogi should live, in one verse. Now, the yogi who has established himself is yogarudha.
He has already gone through the other things we have talked about. He is not attached to the world of objects. He is not attached to his activities.
He reached that state. Now he wants to attain that final connection with the self. So he said, let the yogi try constantly to keep the mind steady.
Probably half an hour a day. So what about the next 23 and a half hours is I let my mind go wherever it wants to go. So what would be more prominent on your mind? The one which youve done in 23 and a half hours or the one you did for half an hour? Of course, the 23 and a half hours will be predominant on your mind.
What will be the nature of your mind, what you do for next 23 and a half hours? So the goal here is to open all 24 hours should be the same. Let the yogi try constantly. Keep the mind steady.
Remaining in solitude. Remaining in solitude. Mentally in solitude.
You may be in a marketplace, but your goal always remains. How my mind is connected, myself is connected. Example of mother in a child.
A mother with an infant child. Child may be in the next room and she is in a kitchen and she is doing whatever she is doing. But her mind is completely attuned to the child.
Even the slightest noise she will recognize. In those days they didnt have those monitors we have here so that you can put a monitor all over the house. But her mind is so tuned to that baby that other people cant hear.
Because mind is constantly focused on where the baby is and what it is doing. A yogi becomes like that he may be doing whatever but his mind is constantly aligned towards his self and the conditions given which will allow him to do this. He doesnt consider himself bound by attachment to all the people around him.
Yata chittatma -- he is balanced in his chitta and atma, the self and the thinking entity. Nirashih -- without any asha (expectation). This is where we get lost, thinking this is maybe not for us; I have too many things to accomplish. But nirashih means he does not seek anything to accomplish outside in the world for his happiness.
He may be accomplishing a lot, but that accomplishment is not going to give him anything more for his connection to his higher self. Hes constantly focused on his connection. Therefore he has no other desire -- getting this or that out of this world will not make him more fit to achieve supreme happiness.
Aparigrahah -- without possessions. All my possessions are of no value when it comes to my understanding of myself. I may be a billionaire, but happiness cannot be bought with billion dollars.
What Im seeking is infinite happiness. I have come to the conclusion anything which is finite is not going to give me happiness. Therefore, acquiring things to get happiness.
I have come to the conclusion is not a good idea. I may acquire things for other reason. To support my body, my mind, my intellect, my relatives, my friends.
For them Im doing this. But not for me to get happiness. Im not buying happiness by acquiring things.
That clear idea is in my mind. My possessing thing is not going to give me happiness. I have come to the conclusion that I have tried this before.

These verses offer the first practical instructions for meditation: sit alone in a secluded place, control the mind, be free from desires and possessions. But the instruction rahasi sthitah - remaining in seclusion - is not merely physical. A mother with an infant in the next room is fully engaged in her tasks, yet her mind is constantly attuned to her child. Similarly, the yogi may be in a crowded marketplace but maintains mental seclusion - an inner focus on the self that is undisturbed by outer activity.
The condition nirashih aparigrahah - without expectations, without possessions - challenges us deeply. We tend to believe that acquiring things will make us complete. If only I had a green card, everything would be solved. But once achieved, new incompleteness arises. The yogi has reached the profound realization that possessions cannot purchase peace. This does not mean abandoning all material support, but rather abandoning the delusion that material acquisition leads to lasting happiness.
Today, examine your relationship with your meditation practice itself. Are you treating it like 30 minutes carved out from the real 23.5 hours of your day? The teaching here is that meditation should gradually infuse all 24 hours. Start by choosing one regular activity - eating breakfast, walking to your car, brushing your teeth - and practice it with the same quality of focused awareness you would bring to formal meditation. This is how the practice expands from the cushion into life.
